source_text:
καὶ ὁ Λουκᾶς…
Καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει· καίτοι πολλῶν εἰληφότων τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ, [[ὡς αὐτὸς πάλιν ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐπιφέρει, φάσκων· »Ὁ λαβὼν τὴν αὐτοῦ μαρτυρίαν ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἀλη- »θής ἐστι«.]] πῶς δὲ οἶόν τε εἶναι ἀληθές, λαμβανόντων αύτοῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν τινῶν, τὸ Καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει«; λυτέον οὖν τὸ ἠπορημένον οὕτως· Ἰησοῦς, ἄνωθεν ἐληλυθὼς λαλῶν τε ἃ ἤκουσε καὶ εἶδεν, ὑψηλοτάτην καὶ πάνυ μεγάλην τὴν μαρτυρίαν λέγει περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ ἑαυτοῦ· καὶ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει ταύτην τὴν μαρτυρίαν ὡς αὐτὸς αὐτὴν λέγει, τῷ τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ἀρχὴν τοῦ λαμβάνειν ἔχοντας πολὺ ἀπολείπεσθαι τοῦ μεγέθους τῆς μαρτυρίας. ὅμως εἰ καὶ οὐδεὶς οἷός τε δέξασθαί ἐστι τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὕτως, ἀλλ᾿ οὐν ἔστι λαβεῖν αὐτὴν ὡς δυνατὸν δέξασθαι τοὺς ἄρτι προσερχομένους τῇ πίστει.
thought_title: No one receives Jesus' testimony as he speaks it
orientation: Origen is resolving a difficulty in John's Gospel: how can it say no one receives Jesus' testimony when many have received it?
pass_a_gloss: And Luke… And his testimony no one receives; although many having received his testimony, [[as]] he himself again John brings in, saying: "The one having received his testimony has sealed that God true is." How then is it possible to be true, some receiving his testimony, the "And his testimony no one receives"? It must be solved then the difficulty thus: Jesus, from above having come and speaking what he heard and saw, highest and very great the testimony speaks about the Father and himself; and no one receives this testimony as he himself speaks it, because the hearers, a beginning of receiving having, fall far short of the greatness of the testimony. Nevertheless even if no one is able to receive his testimony thus, yet it is possible to receive it as it is possible for those just now approaching the faith to receive.

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for μαρτυρία; banned alternatives 'witness' and 'testifying' avoided.
The verb λαμβάνω is rendered 'receive' throughout to preserve the contrast between receiving and not receiving the testimony.
Perfect tense of σφραγίζω rendered with English perfect to mark completed action with present result.
The perfect passive participle of ἀπορέω names the problem as something already posed, matching Origen's method of resolving aporiai.
The perfect participle with adverb preserves the Johannine language of Jesus' heavenly origin.
The middle infinitive expresses the hearers' deficiency relative to the greatness of the testimony.

pass_b_english: [Origen resumes:] And his testimony no one receives. Yet many have received his testimony, as John himself again adds when he says, "The one who received his testimony has sealed that God is true" (John 3:33). How then can it be true, when some do receive his testimony, that "his testimony no one receives" (John 3:32)?

The difficulty raised must be resolved this way. Jesus, who has come from above and speaks what he heard and saw, offers the highest and very great testimony about the Father and himself. No one receives this testimony as he himself speaks it, because the hearers, though they have made a beginning of receiving, fall far short of the greatness of the testimony. Nevertheless, even if no one is able to receive his testimony in that way, still it is possible to receive it insofar as those who are just now approaching the faith are able to receive it.
